source: one definition per statement field, applied identically to filed statements (SEC XBRL companyfacts, us-gaap tags) and to the vendor feed (yfinance 1.7.0 rows); components verified against the universe's FY2025 filings and vendor statements on 2026-09-19
notes: This file is the only place cash, total_debt, delta_nwc and ebit are defined. python/fetch.py reads the vendor rows from it, python/fetch_sec.py the us-gaap tags, and every record's fiscal periods carry a composition per field naming the definition and the components summed; the valuation refuses a record whose composition names a definition this file does not.

Within each list the first present entry wins; 'first complete' means every entry of an alternative must be present. A component absent on both providers is absent, never a substituted zero; only the optional components (short-term investments, short-term borrowings, the current portion of debt on the vendor) may be missing without failing the field.

The cross-check (reference/xbrl_tags.json cross_check_threshold) compares the two providers on the same definitions, so what it still flags is a vendor row that is wrong, lagging or built from a different filed line, never a definitional gap.

refinement_policy: a derived recipe may be refined once per field; a name whose derived value still misses the cross-check threshold, or cannot be checked, is Failed with on_miss. A second refinement requires changing this file on purpose.

ifrs sections (13): the same four definitions on ifrs-full tags for 20-F filers, verified on SAP, Sony, TSMC, Itau, Nu and Kaspi; the recipes are the same, only the components differ. The vendor sections apply to both taxonomies' shadows.
ffo (18): the NAREIT recipe for the Reit class, filed statements only; the vendor has no FFO row, so FFO itself is not cross-checked (its components net income, D&A and dividends are, as before).
shares (19): two definitions, a period's weighted-average diluted count for any flow per share and a point count for market cap; chosen here, never in code.

cash.name: cash_and_short_term_investments
cash.why: A DCF nets debt against non-operating financial assets, and a company's short-term or marketable securities are exactly that; cash-equivalents-only understated equity value on every name that parks its liquidity in securities (Apple by 18.8bn, Microsoft by 55.9bn, Alphabet by 96.1bn at their FY2025 ends). Restricted cash is not available to pay debt: when a filer tags only the total that includes it, the restricted components it tags are deducted (Chevron: 7.285bn less 0.174bn current and 0.818bn noncurrent = 6.293bn, the vendor's balance-sheet cash). The investment tags are taken first-present, not summed, because they overlap for some filers (Apple has tagged both MarketableSecuritiesCurrent and AvailableForSaleSecuritiesDebtSecuritiesCurrent); Coca-Cola files short-term investments (OtherShortTermInvestments 3.602bn) and marketable securities (MarketableSecurities 1.934bn) on separate lines and the vendor sums both, so its cross-check gap of 1.9bn is a known residual of the first-present rule.

not_used: Cash Cash Equivalents And Short Term Investments
notes: The vendor's own subtotal row equals the two components on every name checked (Apple 35.934 + 18.763 = 54.697bn, Coca-Cola 10.270 + 5.536 = 15.806bn) and is not read, so that both providers record the same two components.

Verified FY2025/FY2024: SAP's OtherCurrentFinancialAssets 1.552bn equals the vendor's short-term investments row; TSMC splits its current financial assets by measurement category (192.2 + 102.0 + 0.2bn TWD), summed as one alternative; Sony's OtherCurrentFinancialAssets 145.2bn JPY carries more than the vendor's 28.2bn marketable-securities row and no separate IFRS tag names that line: a known residual.

total_debt.name: financial_debt_excluding_operating_leases
total_debt.why: Financial debt only: long-term debt (current and non-current portions) plus commercial paper and other short-term borrowings. Operating lease liabilities are excluded: under ASC 842 they sit on the balance sheet, but their cost is already inside operating expense, so EBIT and FCFF already bear it and adding the liability to debt as well double-counts (Microsoft 21.9bn, Alphabet 16.0bn, Costco 2.7bn at FY2025). Finance leases stay when the filer folds them into its debt tag (Coca-Cola's and Chevron's LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations). The vendor's Total Debt row is not used: it is Long Term Debt + Current Debt + its two lease rows on all 31 names with a balance sheet, and those lease rows carry the operating lease liability for Microsoft (16.532bn = OperatingLeaseLiabilityNoncurrent), Alphabet (12.744bn) and Costco (2.460bn). The vendor's Current Debt already contains Commercial Paper (Apple: 7.979 + 12.350 Other Current Borrowings = 20.329bn), so commercial paper is never added on top of it.

notes: Recipes, first complete wins: (1) noncurrent + current_total, when the filer tags all debt due within a year as one line (Johnson & Johnson 39.438 + 8.500bn, Chevron 39.781 + 10.918bn); (2) noncurrent + current_long_term, plus short_term_borrowings when tagged (Apple 78.328 + 12.350 + 7.979bn, Microsoft 31.067 + 9.227bn, Coca-Cola 42.119 + 1.822 + 1.495bn); (3) total_including_current, plus short_term_borrowings when tagged. DebtCurrent is the us-gaap sum of the current portion of long-term debt, finance leases due within a year and short-term borrowings, so it is never combined with the other current tags.

Long Term Debt is required; Current Debt is added when the row exists, else the sum of its components when either exists; a name whose vendor statements show no current debt row at all (Alphabet, Costco at FY2025) carries the long-term row alone and the composition says so. The vendor's Long Term Debt excludes finance leases where it shows them separately (Chevron 39.122bn against the filed 39.781bn that folds in 0.659bn of finance leases), a residual the cross-check reports.

Under IFRS 16 every lease is on the balance sheet as LeaseLiabilities, separate from Borrowings, so the operating-lease exclusion holds by construction (SAP 1.684bn EUR, Sony 599.5bn JPY, TSMC 31.8bn TWD stay out). Borrowings is the taxonomy's financial-debt aggregate (SAP 6.150bn = LongtermBorrowings 4.550 + current 1.600); TSMC tags no Borrowings and carries its debt as bonds (926.6 noncurrent + 57.1 current) plus borrowings (31.8 + 59.9), summed by group.

delta_nwc.name: cash_flow_statement_change_in_operating_working_capital
delta_nwc.why: The cash-flow statement's change in operating assets and liabilities is the filed number for cash absorbed by working capital and the conventional FCFF input; the balance-sheet reconstruction used before missed reclassifications, acquisitions and FX (Apple: reconstructed -0.26bn against the filed 25.0bn for FY2025). Positive = cash absorbed. Sign convention, verified on Coca-Cola's FY2025 filing where the aggregate and the components are both tagged: us-gaap IncreaseDecreaseIn<asset> is positive when the asset grows (an outflow, added) and IncreaseDecreaseIn<liability> is positive when the liability grows (an inflow, subtracted); -0.334 + 0.154 + 0.388 + 6.612 + 0.558 - 0.170 = 7.208bn, the filed IncreaseDecreaseInOperatingCapital. The component sum is attempted only when every IncreaseDecreaseIn* tag the filer carries for the period is classified here (asset, liability or excluded); an unclassified tag leaves the field null with a note naming it, so a bank's deposits or an insurer's reserves never become a partial working-capital number. Averaged over at least two periods by the model.

notes: IncreaseDecreaseInOtherOperatingCapitalNet is a net asset (operating assets less operating liabilities), so it is added: Costco FY2025 -0.559 (inventories) + 0.404 x -1 (payables) + -0.801 (other, net) = -1.764bn, the vendor's line to the million.

Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet, Johnson & Johnson and Costco tag components only; Coca-Cola and Chevron tag the aggregate. Chevron's aggregate (0.718bn) excludes the deferred charges and long-term receivables the vendor bundles into its line (1.648bn); the aggregate is the filed operating working capital line and wins.

excluded: deferred tax and pension movements, restricted cash, and Costco's FY2021 IncreaseDecreaseInOutstandingChecksFinancingActivities (a financing flow by its own name) are recognised so they do not block the sum, and never enter it.
The vendor's line is the same cash-flow statement figure with the statement's sign (a release positive), flipped to the boundary's (an increase positive).

Sign convention verified on TSMC FY2024 and SAP FY2025 against the vendor's component rows: AdjustmentsForDecreaseIncreaseInInventories -36.872bn TWD is the vendor's Change In Inventory -36.872 (the statement's sign, a build-up negative), AdjustmentsForIncreaseDecreaseInTradeAccountPayable 17.074 its Change In Account Payable 17.074, SAP's receivables -0.388 its -0.388; the family is cash-flow-signed for assets and liabilities alike, so every component is flipped by sign into the boundary's (an increase in working capital positive). The taxonomy's IncreaseDecreaseInWorkingCapital aggregate is filed only by Itau, a bank, so its sign could not be verified on an operating company and it is not read. Financial-services balances in the family (deposits from customers or banks, loans and advances, held-for-trading assets and liabilities, insurance contract liabilities) are left unclassified on purpose, as on us-gaap: a filer carrying them gets null with a note (Sony's FY2025 20-F still consolidates Sony Bank's deposits), never a partial working capital.

ebit.name: operating_income_else_pretax_plus_interest
ebit.why: Operating income as filed or reported. When the filer tags no OperatingIncomeLoss (Chevron never has; Johnson & Johnson not since FY2014), EBIT is derived from filed tags, never from the vendor: pretax income (the record's canonical pretax_income) plus interest expense, less the non-operating income that pretax carries: the first present of each of interest income, other non-operating income and equity-method earnings, subtracted as filed (income-positive). This is the one refinement the policy allows; the first derived recipe (pretax plus interest) left FY2025's 7.2bn talc-accrual reversal inside Johnson & Johnson's EBIT (33.55bn against the vendor's 25.60bn operating income) and 3.0bn of equity-affiliate earnings inside Chevron's (20.96bn against 16.67bn). A derived EBIT is validated, not assumed: the DCF runs on it only when the record's cross-check finds it within the threshold of the vendor's operating income for the same period; a miss, or no vendor figure to check against, is Failed with refinement_policy.on_miss, and there is no third recipe. Refined: Johnson & Johnson 32.581 + 0.971 - 1.056 - 7.209 = 25.287bn, 1.2% from the vendor; Chevron 19.743 + 1.217 - 3.000 = 17.960bn, 7.7% from the vendor's 16.674bn because its 1.286bn interest and other income is tagged under no standard us-gaap element, so Chevron fails per policy. The vendor path follows the same two recipes with its own rows.

refinement_policy.on_miss: operating income not filed; derived EBIT misses the cross-check

ffo.name: nareit_ffo
ffo.why: A REIT's accounting earnings are dominated by real-estate depreciation on assets that do not depreciate economically, so EPS and an FCFF DCF are mechanically wrong; the industry's measure is FFO per NAREIT: net income + real-estate depreciation and amortisation + impairments of real estate - gains on property sales, from filed tags per period with every component recorded. Net income and depreciation are required (an absent one leaves the field null); impairments and gains are events, not lines every filer has, so an absent one is taken as 0 and the composition says so. AFFO is not derivable: straight-line rent, lease-intangible amortisation and recurring capex are not reliably tagged, so the lens is stated on FFO and every REIT record carries the caveat that FFO overstates distributable cash by what the filer does not tag. Verified FY2025: Realty Income 1058.6 + 2524.2 + 471.3 - 177.6 = 3876.5m (all four tagged); Prologis 3322.3 + 2626.0 (DepreciationAndAmortization; no impairment or gain tag filed since 2018, both taken as 0); Simon Property 4624.3 + 1426.4 (no impairment or gain tag, both taken as 0: its FY2025 net income carries gains no standard tag names, so its FFO reads high).
notes: ifrs-full tags are not mapped: no IFRS REIT is in the universe; a filer with none of the net-income tags leaves ffo null and the model fails naming it.

The distribution rule is recorded, not used: a U.S. REIT must distribute at least 90% of its REIT taxable income excluding net capital gain, jurisdiction-specific; the payout is observed, so the rule is not an input.

shares_for_flows.name: weighted_average_diluted_shares
shares_for_flows.why: A flow accrues over the period and must be divided by the shares that were outstanding while it accrued; a point count taken after year end includes shares issued for acquisitions whose earnings the period does not contain. Realty Income's FFO per share divided by each annual report's cover-page count read 2.10, 3.73, 3.29, 3.98, 4.16 for FY2021 to FY2025 (an 18.7% CAGR) because the February 2022 and 2024 cover pages count the VEREIT and Spirit shares against pre-merger flows; on the period's weighted-average diluted count (908.3m, 863.8m, 693.0m, 612.2m, 414.8m) the growth is low single digits. Every flow per share for a historical period uses this count; the period record carries no point count, so a flow cannot be divided by one.
notes: Verified: Realty Income, Prologis and Simon Property file both tags for every annual period (221, 191 and 215 facts). The basic count is taken only when no diluted one is filed and the tag is recorded. No ifrs-full entry until a flow per share is needed on an IFRS filer.

shares_for_market_cap.name: point_count
shares_for_market_cap.why: Market cap and price times shares need the shares outstanding at a point: effective shares (market cap / price) on the live run, so the ADR ratio cancels; point-in-time, the newest cover-page count filed by the date, else the balance-sheet count at the newest fiscal period end filed by the date (Alphabet files its cover page per share class with a dimension, which companyfacts omits, but its undimensioned CommonStockSharesOutstanding instant), else the record fails naming it. Never a weighted-average count.
notes: The two definitions stay distinct: shares_for_flows is for a period's flow per share, this one for a point.
